results.title: California Memorial Stadium and Simpson Center for Student-Athlete High Performance | 2013-10-16 | Architectural Record
results.snippet: Of the many neoclassical buildings that architect John Galen Howard designed for the University of California, Berkeley, in the early twentieth century, California Memorial Stadium was perhaps the most breathtaking and the most imperiled: from its perch at the base of the Berkeley foothills, the concrete structure—part coliseum, part amphitheater dug into the hillside—offered 73,000 Golden Bears fans sweeping views of San Francisco Bay to the west, but on a site straddling the Hayward Fault. After the University of California's Board of Regents mandated a much-needed seismic revamp in 2005, the university enlisted HNTB Architecture and STUDIOS Architecture to overhaul the 1923 structure, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
